label: NestJS (TypeScript)
description: Modular TypeScript backend — @Module/@Controller/@Injectable triad, DI by token, class-validator DTOs, Swagger from decorators.

vars.name: NestJS
claude_rules: Backend and frontend are **separate concerns** — never mix them in a single agent
No business logic in controllers — controllers delegate to injectable services
Request DTOs carry class-validator decorators and pass through the global `ValidationPipe`

backend-developer.description: TypeScript backend only — NestJS modules/controllers/services, DTOs, guards. Never touches frontend code.
backend-developer.lsp_trace: a DTO or service method to its implementation
context: Backend source lives in `apps/api/src`, one folder per feature
Features are wired as `@Module`s imported by `AppModule`
DTOs live in the feature's `dto/` folder and are validated by the global `ValidationPipe`
rules: Never put business logic in a controller — delegate to an injectable service
Inject providers by token via DI; never `new` a dependency inside a class

scaffold.$comment: Verified end to end: these exact commands produce a project that builds, boots, serves Swagger at /docs, and rejects invalid bodies via the global ValidationPipe.

commands.note: creates apps/api under the root workspaces package.json written in the pre phase
the CLI's sample controller/service are replaced by the first real feature; the app.module.ts convention below drops the imports they left behind
